title: Lumbar spine fusion
description: A lumbar spine fusion is an outpatient surgical procedure where your surgeon removes a damaged disc and fuses two or more vertebrae in your lower back together using bone graft material. This stabilizes your spine and relieves pressure on your spinal nerves that may be causing pain. The procedure takes 1-2 hours, and you may go home the same day or stay overnight. You'll have restrictions on bending, twisting, and lifting for several weeks while your spine heals. Physical therapy helps restore your strength and flexibility. You should expect 4-6 weeks of limited activity before returning to light duty, and 3-6 months before returning to strenuous activities. Most patients experience significant pain relief after the procedure. You may feel some initial fatigue as your body heals. Your fusion restricts motion slightly but provides long-term stability and pain relief.
